title: Electron-Phonon Functional Renormalization Group of Fermi Liquid Instabilities
authors: C. Alexander Baum, Matteo Dürrnagel, Ronny Thomale, Lennart Klebl
abstract: We formulate a functional renormalization group (FRG) ansatz for correlated electron models that incorporates electronic interactions as well as electron-phonon coupling (EPC) stemming from dispersive phonon bands. Particularizing to the RG flow of the electron-electron interaction vertex, we treat phonon- and electron-mediated Fermi liquid instabilities on equal footing as we analyze tentative electronic order parameters related to charge, spin, nematicity, and superconducting pairing. We illustrate the approach at the example of Peierls-type transitions we find for the Hubbard model on the square lattice coupled to acoustic phonon bands. Our method allows to incorporate full electronic and phononic ab initio input, and thus lends itself to the analysis of electronic order from intertwined electronic interactions and EPC at a microscopically most substantiated level.
summary: This work develops an advanced Functional Renormalization Group (FRG) technique to treat correlated electron models that explicitly include electron-phonon coupling. By unifying these interactions, the method allows for a comprehensive analysis of competing electronic instabilities—such as charge density waves or superconductivity—in systems like the Hubbard model on a square lattice. It represents a significant theoretical advance for understanding emergent order in strongly coupled quantum materials.
main_problem: The study aims to formulate a unified theoretical framework for correlated electron systems that treats electronic interactions and electron-phonon coupling (EPC) on equal footing when analyzing Fermi liquid instabilities.
main_result: The functional renormalization group (FRG) approach successfully analyzes the competition between various electronic orders (charge, spin, nematicity, superconductivity) driven by both electronic correlations and EPC in a single formalism.
method: The core method is the Functional Renormalization Group (FRG), which allows for the simultaneous treatment of electronic and phononic degrees of freedom by integrating out phonons to derive retarded interactions.
model_or_system: The primary model analyzed is the Hubbard model on a square lattice coupled to acoustic phonon bands. The Hamiltonian includes terms for electron hopping, on-site repulsion (Hubbard U), and EPC derived from interatomic force constants.
key_observables: Electronic order parameters related to charge, spin, nematicity, and superconducting pairing; phonon softening signatures.
important_parameters: The Hubbard interaction strength (U), the electron-phonon coupling constant (g), and lattice geometry/dispersion relations ($\omega_{n,\mathbf{q}}$).
main_assumptions: Initial treatment assumes the harmonic approximation for phonons, and some derivations simplify by ignoring the renormalization of the retarded interaction ($V_{R,\Lambda}$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate band structures (Hubbard model), schematic representations of EPC from lattice perturbations, and flow diagrams showing how the static vertex renormalizes across different coupling channels.
paper_structure: The paper develops the FRG ansatz for coupled electron-phonon systems, derives the necessary retarded interactions by integrating out phonons, analyzes the renormalization flow of the two-particle vertex in various channels (P, C, D), and applies this to the Hubbard model example.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter correlations, the use of advanced many-body techniques like FRG for coupled quantum systems provides methodological insights applicable to open quantum systems where coupling to a bosonic bath (phonons/environment) is crucial.
